topic: cache consistency and cross-service stale data

method.selection: Three first-party engineering accounts, chosen for different consistency contracts and lifecycle assumptions rather than popularity.
method.deduplication: Compared lane article inventories, docs/research/consistency-primary-sources.md, the research tree, and relevant skill references. Exact article URLs/title fragments were absent before this extension.
excluded_prior_deep_reads: Amazon Builders' Library: Caching challenges and strategies
method.access: Public first-party HTML; no authentication, purchases, copied article bodies, or source-code downloads.
method.inference_policy: Practice cards are original transfer proposals. Article mechanisms require their stated storage and topology assumptions; none is claimed to be a universal cache design.
method.scope_limit: Read technical body text and captions. Diagrams and performance charts were not independently inspected; no numerical performance claim is adopted. Documentation reads are selected sections, not entire manuals. No code, skills, fixtures, or evaluations changed.

articles.title: Meet Chrono, our scalable, consistent, metadata caching solution
articles.read_scope: Technical body from motivation through design, Panda API prerequisites, read/write protocol, argument for correctness, validation, and lessons. Navigation/advertising excluded.
articles.synthesis: A lossy value cache can be safe only because a separate authority and storage-enforced bounds validate it; the boot sequence is part of that proof.
articles.limitations: Proprietary Panda APIs; ordinary SQL timestamps or Redis metadata do not automatically satisfy its assumptions.

articles.title: How Uber Serves over 150 Million Reads per Second from Integrated Cache with Stronger Consistency Guarantees
articles.read_scope: Technical body: architecture recap, stale-value causes and magnitude, conditional-write changes, invalidation flow, measurement, and conclusion. Linked earlier article not counted/read deeply.
articles.synthesis: CDC, version-aware cache operations, and write-path invalidation strengthen practical behavior without removing every successful-write/stale-read history.
articles.limitations: Custom Docstore/Flux integration. Its TTL and hit-rate choices are workload evidence, not defaults to copy.

articles.title: Quicksilver v2: evolution of a globally distributed key-value store (Part 1)
articles.read_scope: Technical body: proxy/replica motivation, working sets, persistence/eviction, asynchronous replication, historical reads, retained recent updates, negative lookups, discovery, and results. Part 2 not counted/read deeply.
articles.synthesis: Partial replicas must preserve the reader's intended cut, including absence, when load balancing across differing replication positions.
articles.limitations: Integrated Quicksilver replication, custom RocksDB storage, and workload-specific retention. No portable two-hour retention recommendation.

crosschecks.title: Redis WAIT command contract
crosschecks.version_scope: Current command documentation, command available since Redis 3.0; nonblocking-context behavior noted since 7.0
crosschecks.read_scope: Acknowledgement count, timeout, connection scope, consistency caveat, implementation, and examples.
crosschecks.finding: WAIT does not make Redis strongly consistent or guarantee failover preserves every replicated write; callers must inspect the returned count.
crosschecks.transfer: Do not substitute replication acknowledgement for proof that correctness metadata survives failover.

crosschecks.title: etcd API
crosschecks.read_scope: Response header, key/value metadata, revisions, Range request and response.
crosschecks.finding: Range revision selects a historical view and compacted history fails; key version resets on deletion, while store revision orders mutations.
crosschecks.transfer: Distinguish exact snapshot identity, minimum dependency context, per-key counters, and filters.

crosschecks.title: Debezium connector for PostgreSQL
crosschecks.read_scope: Incremental snapshot collision handling/window, read-only snapshot prerequisites, supported topology, startup/history failures, cluster failure, and Kafka Connect crash recovery.
crosschecks.finding: Snapshot buffers discard a row read when a live event for that key supersedes it; restarts can duplicate events and missing retained history requires recovery.
crosschecks.transfer: Use the connector's documented baseline/stream protocol; do not assume output ordering alone fixes downstream parallel effects.

crosschecks.title: PostgreSQL Logical Decoding Concepts
crosschecks.access: public documentation, complete short concepts page
crosschecks.read_scope: Sections 47.2.1 through 47.2.5, especially slots, synchronization, and exported snapshots.
crosschecks.finding: Slot positions can rewind after crashes. Exported snapshots define the baseline preceding a change stream; failover resume requires suitable persistent synchronized slots.
crosschecks.transfer: Validate snapshot/stream continuity and repeated delivery; a recreated slot is not proof historical changes survived.

crosschecks.title: etcd Disaster recovery
crosschecks.access: public documentation; prior section reading crosschecked against existing research
crosschecks.read_scope: Revision rollback and restored revision bump with compaction; already analyzed in recovery-caches-and-canaries.md, not a new deep read.
crosschecks.finding: Surviving watchers can retain state beyond a restored snapshot; the documented revision procedure forces rebuilding.
crosschecks.transfer: Already covered in recovery-validation; no additional generic cache-flush recommendation.

practices.trigger: A database write and cache invalidation have different failure boundaries.
practices.failure: Success is mistaken for guaranteed freshness when cache work failed.
practices.mechanism: Name commit, cache acknowledgement, dependent-read behavior, and gap repair separately; preserve known committed outcomes.
practices.limits: Choose semantics per operation; stronger freshness can require waiting, routing, or explicit unavailability.
practices.counterexample: An availability-oriented catalogue may accept documented lag.
practices.verification: Commit, fail invalidation, then read through another service; include negative caching followed by insertion.
practices.novelty: Existing gap explanation; new explicit acknowledgement/failure decision and verification.

practices.trigger: Freshness authority restarts while cache values or old fills survive.
practices.failure: Initialization temporarily loses the evidence required to reject stale data.
practices.mechanism: Gate admission on restored validation authority; include startup in the invariant and failure model.
practices.limits: A strict protocol requires every writer and the store's actual guarantees; do not invent portable commit timestamps.
practices.counterexample: A disposable cache with permitted staleness needs no custom freshness service.
practices.verification: Read before initialization, after safe admission, and during delayed-fill delivery.
practices.novelty: Restart/loss already covered; explicit admission and startup schedule absent.

practices.trigger: A projection rebuild reads a baseline while source writes continue.
practices.failure: A delayed baseline row overwrites a live update or resurrects a deletion.
practices.mechanism: Use supported source-cut and collision rules; persist recoverable progress and validate catch-up before admission.
practices.limits: Connector guarantees do not cover arbitrary downstream concurrency; unavailable history requires reconciliation or rebuilding.
practices.counterexample: A verified quiescent rebuild need not implement an online collision buffer.
practices.verification: Pause a snapshot row, stream its deletion, release the row, then restart processing; deletion and progress remain correct.
practices.novelty: Substantive gap: existing known-baseline requirement lacks the online handoff protocol.

practices.trigger: One operation requires a common historical view across cache misses.
practices.failure: A newer response changes that view; an older replica omits required state.
practices.mechanism: Carry the requested cut, serve valid history including absence, and define unavailable-history behavior.
practices.limits: Requires comparable source positions and retained history; fixed retention from another workload is insufficient.
practices.counterexample: Read-your-writes can accept a later version without requiring one exact snapshot.
practices.verification: Use replicas ahead/behind the cut, delete/recreate, and compacted history.
practices.novelty: Minimum context and monotonic reads exist; exact-cut conditional guidance is new.
